Winsome

WIN-sum · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Winsome is charming and appealing in a simple, wholesome way.

The stray dog's winsome, limp-tailed wag won over even the shelter's sternest volunteer.

Worked Example

The new intern's winsome habit of remembering everyone's coffee order made her instantly popular around the office.

Nothing about her was flashy or dramatic -- she was simply likable and appealing in a warm, easy way, which is exactly what winsome describes.

Antonyms

repellent

repellent: causing dislike or disgust

off-putting

off-putting: unpleasant or discouraging

How Strong Is It? — pleasant → winsome → irresistible

pleasant vs. winsome

pleasant vs. winsome: Something pleasant is simply agreeable, without the special warmth or charm of something winsome.

irresistible vs. winsome

irresistible vs. winsome: Something irresistible is so charming it's genuinely impossible to resist, even more captivating than merely winsome.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — win-

root — win-: joy, delight (from Old English wynn, a word now obsolete; its spelling survives here as win-)

suffix — -some

suffix — -some: characterized by; tending to (Old English -sum)

Put it together

Put it together: Winsome is built from win- ('joy, delight,' from Old English wynn, a word now obsolete -- its spelling survives here as win-) + -some ('characterized by') -- literally 'characterized by joy.' The old root didn't survive into modern English as its own word, but the -some suffix lives on in plenty of familiar words.

Use the root in a new word: awesome

Use the root in a new word: awesome: The view from the mountain peak was simply awesome.

Word Choice

Winsome describes a gentle, wholesome kind of charm -- a smile, a manner, a personality -- rather than the bold, showy appeal of something ostentatious or gaudy.
